title: Function-field spectra in a dominant affine transition limit
statement:
Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category and $X:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a diagram of
integral quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $S$ be integral
and let $\alpha:S\to X$ be a limiting cone with every projection $\alpha_i$ dominant.
There exist $K:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$, a limiting cone
$b:\operatorname{Spec}k(S)\to K$, a natural transformation $t:K\to X$, and
isomorphisms $e_i:K_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}k(X_i)$. All $K_i$ are quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and the transition maps of $K$ are affine. Writing $\iota$ and
$\iota_i$ for the canonical maps from the spectra of the function fields to $S$ and
$X_i$, respectively, one has $e_i^{-1}t_i=\iota_i$ and $b_i t_i=\iota\alpha_i$.

source.place: Tag 0EZJ, proof of Lemma 58.31.9, function-field calculation underlying the assertion that the generic fibre is a limit

proof.text: A dominant map of irreducible schemes sends the generic point to the generic point: apply IsGenericPoint.image to genericPoint_spec and use DenseRange.closure_range. Each transition X.map f is dominant by IsDominant.of_comp and the cone identity. Construct the spectrum maps from the actual generic stalk maps, transported by eqToHom along the generic-point equality. Scheme.SpecMap_stalkMap_fromSpecStalk proves compatibility with the generic inclusions. Cancel these monomorphisms to prove the functor and natural-transformation laws. This constructs K, b and t, with e the identity isomorphisms.

For a point s of S whose projections are all the stage generic points, Mathlib isBasis_preimage_isAffineOpen gives a basis of inverse images of stage affine opens. Every basis neighbourhood of the generic point of S contains s, since its image at the relevant stage equals the image of that generic point. Thus s specializes to the generic point. The generic point specializes to s; T0 separation gives equality. In particular, for any cone z on K, lift its composite with t through the limiting cone on X. Every point of this lifted morphism maps to the generic point of S, because each stage spectrum is the spectrum of a field and has exactly one point.

Any morphism g:T to S whose image consists of the generic point factors uniquely through every affine neighbourhood of that point. Use IsOpenImmersion.lift for the factors; cancel the open inclusions to prove their compatibility. The universal property of the generic stalk spectrum as the limit of these affine neighbourhoods gives a morphism T to Spec k(S) whose composite with the canonical generic inclusion is g. Apply this construction to each cone on K. Cancel the stage generic inclusions and use the limit identities on X to prove the cone factorization identities. Cancel the generic inclusion into S and use uniqueness for the limit on X to prove uniqueness. This proves that the explicitly constructed cone b is limiting without a separate fraction-field colimit calculation.

Each K.obj i is literally Spec k(X_i), so Mathlib affine-scheme instances give CompactSpace and QuasiSeparatedSpace. Every transition between these affine schemes is affine. The identity isomorphisms give the first comparison equality by Category.id_comp; the stalk-map compatibility established in the first step gives the second comparison equality.

theorem exists_dominant_function_field_limit {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I]
    [IsCofiltered I] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S]
    (X : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsIntegral (X.obj i)]
    (hXqc : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X.obj i)) (hXqs : ∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (X.obj i))
    (hXa : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (X.map f))
    (α : (Functor.const I).obj S ⟶ X) (hα : IsLimit (Cone.mk S α))
    (hdom : ∀ i, IsDominant (α.app i)) :
    ∃ (K : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (b : (Functor.const I).obj (Spec S.functionField) ⟶ K)
      (t : K ⟶ X) (e : ∀ i, K.obj i ≅ Spec (X.obj i).functionField)
      (hb : IsLimit (Cone.mk (Spec S.functionField) b)),
      (∀ i, CompactSpace (K.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (K.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (K.map f)) ∧
      (∀ i, (e i).inv ≫ t.app i = (X.obj i).fromSpecStalk (genericPoint (X.obj i))) ∧
      (∀ i, b.app i ≫ t.app i = S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S) ≫ α.app i)
